key_insight: mmRUDEs make neural constitutive models more stable, thermodynamically admissible, and interpretable by combining a multi-mode tensorial backbone with conditioning and projection safeguards.
engineering_relevance: The framework improves data-driven rheology models for predicting complex polymer flow behavior under unseen conditions, supporting CFD and process design.
method: Use a multi-mode RUDE with a frame-indifferent tensor-basis constitutive backbone.
Apply logarithmic input compression and a split-network architecture to improve training conditioning.
Enforce the Clausius–Duhem inequality with a differentiable projection layer and summarize learned behavior with the rheome.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on LAOS data and validated on synthetic multi-mode Giesekus and experimental silicone melt cases, remaining stable and accurate in steady shear, transient stress growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The added projection and architecture complexity may increase implementation effort and requires careful tuning to preserve stability without overconstraining model expressiveness.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
